//: These files are ES modules, and nothing but this file says so.
//why: pil-resize.js uses `export`. The browser knows that from the import that
fetches it, but Node decides by the nearest package.json -- which was the
repo root, declaring "type": "commonjs". So Node parsed it as CommonJS and
threw. Two CI steps had been failing on it since the monorepo restructure:
the Python job's browser-preprocessing parity (SyntaxError: Named export
'preprocess' not found) and the backend job's headless feature parity
This is the fix rather than renaming to .mjs, because the file is served to
the browser at the URL /js/pil-resize.js from three places in the app and a
rename would mean changing a shipped path to satisfy a test runner. A
package.json here changes nothing that is served -- the browser never asks
for it -- and every file in this directory really is a module.
